title: Universal closedness of algebraic-space morphisms is detected by affine scheme tests
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the usual point-space topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose that for every affine scheme $T$ over $S$ and every morphism $T\to Y$, the map $|X\times_YT|\to|T|$ is closed, meaning that the image of each closed subset is closed. Then $f$ is universally closed: for every algebraic space $Y\prime$ over $S$ and every morphism $Y\prime\to Y$, the map $|X\times_Y Y\prime|\to|Y\prime|$ is closed.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary algebraic space $Z$ over $S$ and morphism $Z\to Y$. Put $P=X\times_Y Z$ and let $p:P\to Z$ be its projection; these exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. By [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], choose a representable surjective etale atlas $q:W\to Z$ with $W=\coprod_{i\in I}W_i$ and every $W_i$ an affine $S$-scheme. Write $q_i:W_i\to Z$ for its restriction. The same cited statement identifies the topology on $|Z|$ with the quotient topology for $|q|$.

source.place: Tag 03IT (lemma-universally-closed-local), proof of (3) implies (4), applied directly to an arbitrary base change.

proof.text: Let $C\subseteq|P|$ be closed and put $D=|p|(C)$. For each $i$, form $P_i=P\times_ZW_i$, with projections $r_i:P_i\to P$ and $p_i:P_i\to W_i$, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The fibre-product universal property identifies $P_i$ with $X\times_YW_i$: a compatible triple $(x,z,w)$ is sent to $(x,w)$, with inverse $(x,w)\mapsto(x,q_i(w),w)$. This isomorphism induces a homeomorphism, since both inverse morphisms induce continuous point maps by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Set $C_i=|r_i|^{-1}(C)$. The continuity clause of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] makes $C_i$ closed. Since $W_i$ is an affine $S$-scheme and its map to $Y$ is the composite through $Z$, the hypothesis of the item says that $D_i=|p_i|(C_i)$ is closed in $|W_i|$.

source.place: Tag 03IT (lemma-universally-closed-local), proof of (3) implies (4), applied directly to an arbitrary base change.

proof.text: For each $i$ we have $|q_i|^{-1}(D)=D_i$. One inclusion follows from $p\circ r_i=q_i\circ p_i$. Conversely, if $w\in|W_i|$ and $|q_i|(w)=|p|(x)$ for some $x\in C$, apply the surjectivity of $|P\times_ZW_i|\to|P|\times_{|Z|}|W_i|$ in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. It gives $v\in|P_i|$ projecting to $(x,w)$. Thus $v\in C_i$ and $w=|p_i|(v)\in D_i$. This uses surjectivity onto the set-theoretic fibre product, not an identification of that set with the points of the algebraic-space fibre product.

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), applied to the square P_i = P times_Z W_i; makes explicit the descent inference in Tag 03IT.

proof.text: Consequently $|q|^{-1}(D)$ is closed in $|W|$: on every open disjoint summand $|W_i|$ its complement is the open set $|W_i|\setminus D_i$, and the complement on $|W|$ is their union. By the quotient-topology clause of [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], $D$ is closed in $|Z|$. This is the topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology]: an open set for that final topology pulls back to an open set along the atlas, while a quotient-open set pulls back openly along every etale scheme-source map by the continuity clause of the cover node. Since $C$ and $Z\to Y$ were arbitrary, every algebraic-space base change of $f$ is closed, as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NP-acacec6eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item: statement unchanged, no new nodes, and a four-step proof of Stacks Tag 03IT (3)⇒(1). The proof applies the source's chart argument for (3)⇒(4) directly to an arbitrary base change Z→Y, which is valid because the argument never uses the atlas V. Steps: (1) the fibre-product node forms P=X×_Y Z, and the cover node gives an atlas W=⊔W_i of affine S-schemes with the quotient topology on |Z|. (2) P_i=P×_Z W_i is identified with X×_Y W_i by the universal property. Point maps are continuous, so this is a homeomorphism compatible with the projections to W_i, and the affine hypothesis makes |p_i|(C_i) closed. (3) |q_i|^{-1}(D)=D_i: one inclusion is functoriality of point maps, the other uses only the 03H4 surjectivity clause of point-open-calculus. (4) This step is genuinely elementary: the complement is a union of opens in the disjoint summands, so D is closed in the quotient topology. That topology equals the final topology of def-a1-space-point-topology in both directions, by the atlas and by the continuity clause of the cover node. Sources read: 03IT and definition-closed (spaces-morphisms.tex), 03H4 and 03FX (spaces-properties.tex). Edge cases checked: empty Z, infinitely many components, Z or P_i not a scheme, and the non-injective point fibre product; all fine. Duplicate search over the DAG ('universally closed', 03IT, universally-closed-local) found no node stating this criterion. They are generic point-topology facts, not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so I accept them.
